body:
## Pull request overview

Adds a new “Utilities & Tools” documentation section and publishes initial docs pages for the project’s developer tooling packages.

**Changes:**
- Introduces a new `utilities/` docs section with pages for CLI, create-plugin, runner, data-objectstack, and the VS Code extension
- Wires the new section into docs navigation (`content/docs/meta.json`) and the main docs landing page
- Adds cross-links from existing guides (architecture, plugins) to the new utilities docs

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 11 out of 11 changed files in this pull request and generated 34 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx | New CLI documentation page (commands, schema formats, config, examples) |
| content/docs/utilities/create-plugin.mdx | New create-plugin documentation page (scaffold workflow, examples, conventions) |
| content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx | New ObjectStack adapter documentation page (installation, API, examples) |
| content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx | New Runner documentation page (usage, structure, extension guidance) |
| content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx | New VS Code extension documentation page (features, commands, settings) |
| content/docs/utilities/index.md | New utilities landing page aggregating all tools |
| content/docs/utilities/meta.json | Adds utilities section page ordering |
| content/docs/meta.json | Adds `utilities` to top-level docs navigation |
| content/docs/index.md | Adds utilities section to the main docs homepage |
| content/docs/guide/plugins.md | Adds links from plugin guide to utilities docs |
| content/docs/guide/architecture.md | Adds utilities list and link in the architecture guide |
</details>

The prompt list doesn’t match what the CLI actually asks. The implementation (`packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts`) prompts for name (if missing), description, and author only—no component name/type or license. Please adjust the documented prompts to match the real ones.
```suggestion

```

This suggests importing plugins in `src/main.tsx`, but the current runner imports plugins in `src/App.tsx` (`packages/runner/src/App.tsx`). Please update the instructions to point to the correct file (or change the runner to import from `main.tsx`).

This section describes a React `ObjectStackProvider`, but the package currently exports `ObjectStackAdapter` / `createObjectStackAdapter` (no provider component) in `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` and `packages/data-objectstack/README.md`. Please rewrite the quick start to show creating the adapter and passing it into the renderer (per the existing package README).

The dependency list is incorrect: `@object-ui/create-plugin` uses `commander` + `prompts` (and does not depend on Inquirer or Ora). See `packages/create-plugin/package.json`. Please update this list to reflect the actual dependencies.
```suggestion
- **commander** - CLI command and argument parsing
- **prompts** - Interactive prompts
- **Chalk** - Terminal colors
```

`Export to React` is documented as copying code to the clipboard, but the implementation opens a new editor tab with generated TSX (`packages/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts`, `exportToReact`). Please update the usage text to match actual behavior.

The generated project layout shown here doesn’t match the tool’s output. The generator writes into `./packages/plugin-<name>/...` (see `packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts`, `targetDir = path.join(process.cwd(), 'packages', fullPackageName)`) and generates `src/<Name>Impl.tsx`, not `AwesomeComponent.tsx`. Please update this structure section to match the actual scaffold.

The directory structure shown here doesn’t match the actual `packages/runner/src` layout (there is no `src/schemas/` or `src/components/`; schemas live under `src/app-data/` and are loaded via `LocalBundleLoader` in `packages/runner/src/lib/MetadataLoader.ts`). Please update this tree to reflect the real structure.
```suggestion
│   ├── app-data/                # Example schemas and local metadata bundles
│   │   ├── dashboard.json
│   │   ├── kanban.json
│   │   └── charts.json
│   ├── lib/
│   │   └── MetadataLoader.ts    # Loads schemas via LocalBundleLoader
│   ├── App.tsx                  # Main application
│   └── main.tsx                 # Entry point
├── public/                      # Static assets
```

The settings documented here don’t match the extension’s contributed configuration. In `packages/vscode-extension/package.json`, `objectui.preview.port` defaults to `3000` (not `5173`), and there is no `objectui.validation.severity` or `objectui.snippets.enabled` setting. Please update this section to list only the settings that actually exist.

This CLI example uses `--schema`, but the current CLI expects the schema file as a positional argument (`objectui dev [schema]`) and doesn’t define a `--schema` flag (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`). Please update the command example to avoid a copy/paste failure for readers.
```suggestion
  npx @object-ui/cli dev dashboard.json
```

The CLI is documented as supporting `OBJECTUI_*` environment variables, but there’s no env var handling in the implementation (`packages/cli/src` has no `OBJECTUI_` usage). Please either add env var support or remove these docs to keep them accurate.
```suggestion

```

`BaseComponentSchema` is referenced here, but it doesn’t exist in `@object-ui/types` (the base type is `BaseSchema`). This snippet won’t type-check as written; please update to the correct type(s) exported by `@object-ui/types`.
```suggestion
import type { BaseSchema } from '@object-ui/types'

export interface AwesomeComponentSchema extends BaseSchema {
```

This documents `.create-plugin.config.js` customization, but the CLI implementation does not load or apply any external config file (no references in `packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts`). Please remove this section or implement config support.
```suggestion
## Plugin Naming Conventions
```

The package is labeled “not published to npm”, but `packages/runner/package.json` is not `private: true`, and `packages/runner/README.md` documents installing it (`pnpm add @object-ui/runner`) and programmatic usage. Please correct the package status here to match the repository’s current publishing model.
```suggestion
**Type:** Application (published to npm)  
```

The plugin list here drops the npm scope (e.g., `plugin-grid`), but the actual packages are scoped (`@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `@object-ui/plugin-form`, etc.). Please update the names to match the real package names to avoid confusion when users try to install them.
```suggestion
- **@object-ui/plugin-grid** - Data grids with ObjectStack queries
- **@object-ui/plugin-form** - Forms with ObjectStack CRUD
- **@object-ui/plugin-kanban** - Kanban boards with ObjectStack data
- **@object-ui/plugin-calendar** - Calendars with ObjectStack events
- **@object-ui/plugin-gantt** - Gantt charts with ObjectStack tasks
- **@object-ui/plugin-map** - Maps with ObjectStack locations
```

This example imports `ObjectStackProvider` from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, but that symbol does not exist in the package (it exports `ObjectStackAdapter` / `createObjectStackAdapter`). Please update the snippet to use `createObjectStackAdapter(...)` per `packages/data-objectstack/README.md` and the actual exports in `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`.
```suggestion
import { createObjectStackAdapter } from '@object-ui/data-objectstack'
import { SchemaRendererProvider } from '@object-ui/react'

const objectStack = createObjectStackAdapter({
  apiUrl: 'https://api.example.com',
  apiKey: 'your-api-key',
})

function App() {
  return (
    <SchemaRendererProvider dataSource={objectStack}>
      <SchemaRenderer schema={schema} />
    </SchemaRendererProvider>
```

This workflow assumes `create-plugin` generates a top-level `my-plugin/` folder, but the current generator writes into `./packages/plugin-<name>/...` (see `packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts`). Please update the `cd` path and wording so users land in the correct directory after generation.
```suggestion
cd packages/plugin-my-plugin/src
```

This example uses a dynamic Tailwind class name (`text-${color}-600`), which won’t be picked up by Tailwind’s class scanning unless users add a safelist. For docs/templates, prefer a fixed mapping (e.g., enum -> className) or variants via `class-variance-authority` to avoid generating broken styles.
```suggestion
  const colorClassMap: Record<string, string> = {
    blue: 'text-blue-600',
    red: 'text-red-600',
    green: 'text-green-600',
    yellow: 'text-yellow-600',
  }

  const colorClass = colorClassMap[color] ?? colorClassMap.blue

  return (
    <div className={`p-4 ${colorClass}`}>
```

These sections continue to reference `ObjectStackProvider` / `useObjectStack` and CRA-style `REACT_APP_*` env vars, none of which exist in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` today. Please replace with the adapter’s actual config keys (`baseUrl`, `token`, `cache`) and, if you want to show env vars, use a bundler-agnostic example (or Vite-style `import.meta.env`).

The `dev` command options here don’t match the implementation: in `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` it takes an optional positional `[schema]` argument (default `app.json`), the port default is `3000` (not `5173`), and `--host` expects a host value (`-h, --host <host>`), not a boolean. Please align the documented flags/defaults with the actual CLI.

The “This will” list is inaccurate for the current generator: `packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts` does not install dependencies or initialize a git repository (it only prints next steps). Please update these steps (or add the missing behaviors).
```suggestion
3. Print clear next steps (like installing dependencies and initializing a git repository)

### Interactive Prompts
```

The Runner is described as “Pre-configured – All official plugins included”, but the app currently imports/includes only `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` and `@object-ui/plugin-charts` (`packages/runner/src/App.tsx`). Please reword this to avoid implying all plugins are bundled.
```suggestion
- 📦 **Pre-configured** - Bundled with core official plugins (e.g. Kanban, Charts)
```

The command name/title and shortcut info here doesn’t match the extension manifest. In `packages/vscode-extension/package.json`, the command titles are “Object UI: Open Preview” / “Open Preview to the Side”, and the extension does not contribute any default keybindings. Please update this section to reflect the real command names and remove (or clearly mark) the shortcut defaults.
```suggestion
### `Object UI: Open Preview`

Opens a live preview of your schema in a VS Code editor tab.

**Usage:**
1. Open a `.json` or `.objectui.json` file
2. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Shift+P` (Mac)
3. Type "Object UI: Open Preview"
4. Run the command to open the preview

> Note: The extension does not define a default keyboard shortcut for this command. You can add your own keybinding in VS Code Keyboard Shortcuts.

### `Open Preview to the Side`

Opens a live preview of your schema in a side-by-side editor column.

**Usage:**
1. Open a `.json` or `.objectui.json` file
2. Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd+Shift+P` (Mac)
3. Type "Open Preview to the Side"
4. Run the command to open the preview beside your schema

> Note: The extension does not define a default keyboard shortcut for this command. You can add your own keybinding in VS Code Keyboard Shortcuts.
```

`objectui init` does not support `--schema` and it doesn’t “initialize from a schema” as written here. In `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, `init` only accepts `--template` and generates a sample app (positional arg is the app name). Please update this section to match the actual CLI interface (or add `--schema` support in the CLI).

The `build` flags listed here (`--outDir`, `--minify`, `--sourcemap`) don’t exist in the current CLI. `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` defines `-o, --out-dir <dir>` and `--clean` for `objectui build`. Please update the option names and examples to match.

This section documents an `objectui.config.js` file, but the CLI currently doesn’t read any config file (`packages/cli/src` has no references to `objectui.config`). Please remove this section or implement config loading to avoid misleading users.
```suggestion
Configuration via a project-level config file (such as `objectui.config.js`) is not yet supported by the ObjectUI CLI.

For now, configure CLI behavior using command-line flags (for example, `--port`, `--host`, or build-related options) and environment variables supported by the underlying tooling (Node, Vite, etc.).

This section will be updated once file-based configuration is officially supported in `@object-ui/cli`.
```

This “Add Custom Routes” example assumes `react-router-dom`, but the runner app does not use React Router for routing (`packages/runner/src/App.tsx` uses `window.history.pushState`). Please either update the example to match the current navigation approach or explicitly state it’s an optional alternative with additional dependencies.

`ErrorBoundary` is imported from `@object-ui/components` in this snippet, but that component doesn’t appear to exist/export from the components package. Please either change the example to a standard React error boundary implementation or add/link to the actual error-boundary component if one exists.

The file association rules listed here don’t match the extension: it explicitly targets `*.objectui.json` and `*.oui.json` (and treats `app.json` as a schema in code), but it does not special-case `schema.json` or “any JSON with type=app” in its contributions. Please align this list with `packages/vscode-extension/package.json` and `isObjectUISchema()` in `packages/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts`.
```suggestion
- `*.objectui.json` – ObjectUI schema files
- `*.oui.json` – Alternate ObjectUI schema files
- `app.json` – Application-level schema entrypoints
```

This table lists “Default keyboard shortcuts”, but the extension does not contribute any `keybindings` in `packages/vscode-extension/package.json`. Please remove the “default shortcuts” table or change it to “suggested shortcuts” and show how to configure them manually.

The `dataSource` example shape is inconsistent with the actual `DataFetchConfig` type: `dataSource.api` can be a string or an `APIRequest` object (`packages/types/src/api-types.ts`), so `method` should be inside `api` when you need it (instead of being a sibling key). As written, `method` would be ignored by strict consumers/validators.
```suggestion
    "api": {
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/api/users",
      "method": "GET"
    }
```

`@objectstack/client` is documented as a peer dependency that must be installed separately, but `packages/data-objectstack/package.json` lists it under `dependencies`. Please update this note to reflect the actual dependency type/installation behavior.

The schema examples here use a custom `dataSource: { type: "objectstack", object, query... }` shape and `objectstack.create` actions, but `@object-ui/data-objectstack` is a programmatic `DataSource` adapter and does not define/consume these schema fields. Please align this section with the real API (`createObjectStackAdapter({ baseUrl, token, cache })`) and the actual query model (`QueryParams` with `$filter`, `$select`, etc.).

`objectui preview` is documented here, but there is no `preview` command in the CLI (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`). The closest equivalent is `objectui start` (production server) after `objectui build`. Please either document `start` instead, or implement a `preview` command.
